notes: Difficult shared cases for the design/change cluster plus systematic-debugging (the close neighbor for 'flaky failure' hardening cases). The discriminations: WHAT-to-decide (requirements), whether the current shape is right (architecture-review), HOW-to-execute an approved direction (implementation-planning), test-first hardening (quality-hardening), and behavior-preserving reduction (reduce-code-size).

cases.prompt: Every change to billing touches the same five modules and the team thinks the boundaries may be wrong. Review the current shape and recommend whether we should restructure it.
cases.notes: Pair A: deciding whether to restructure. Paired case flips to execution planning.

cases.prompt: We've already decided to split billing behind an internal API. Work out the migration sequence, intermediate states, rollback points, and verification.
cases.notes: Pair B: planning HOW after the decision. The word 'migration' must not route to architecture-review.

cases.prompt: Our customers keep asking to download their invoices as PDF, but we're not sure whether to build it in-app, email it, or use a third-party service. Help us figure out what to build.
cases.notes: No design exists yet; the job is requirements/approach selection, not architecture review of an existing system and not an execution plan.

cases.prompt: The design for our new billing webhook system is settled and was approved last week. The decision and design doc live in docs/design/billing-webhooks.md. Give me an execution-ready implementation plan an engineer can carry out without re-deriving the design.
cases.notes: Design vocabulary everywhere; the deliverable is the execution plan from an approved design.

cases.prompt: Our payment retry logic has an occasional flaky failure under concurrency. Add a regression test that reproduces the race, then make the minimal fix and confirm the gate is green.
cases.notes: Debugging vocabulary (flaky failure) but the dominant job is test-first hardening with a confirmed-red regression test, not root-cause diagnosis alone.

cases.prompt: The module utils/data_transform.py is about 900 lines and I suspect a lot of it is dead or duplicated logic. Measure the size first, then do a behavior-preserving reduction.
cases.notes: Review vocabulary (dead/duplicated logic) but the deliverable is a measured, behavior-preserving shrink, not a findings report.

cases.prompt: I have a loose idea for a feature that lets users export all their data. I'm not sure what the behavior should be or which approach is best yet, but once we figure that out I want a build plan.
cases.notes: Two intents in one message; the oracle reflects the currently dominant one (requirements first). A router that jumps to planning is wrong.

cases.prompt: This part of the system has become painful to change. What should we do?
cases.notes: Real partial evidence: could be architecture (changeability), could be implementation (the pain is a known defect), could be requirements (the direction is undecided). Clarification or a documented tie-breaker is required; no single owner is defensible without it.

cases.prompt: The checkout service is flaky and users complain it sometimes double-charges. Find the root cause before we change anything.
cases.notes: Pair A: diagnose first. The paired case flips to hardening after the cause is known.

cases.prompt: We found the root cause of the double-charge: the retry and the webhook handler race. Harden it: add the failing regression test, make the minimal fix, and confirm the gate is green.
cases.notes: Pair B: the cause is established; the job is test-first hardening, not diagnosis.

cases.prompt: The architecture is already decided. I need the exact implementation sequence, the intermediate states, and the verification plan for each phase.
cases.notes: 'Architecture' appears but the decision is made; the deliverable is the execution plan.

cases.prompt: Can you look at this subsystem and tell me whether the design is the reason every change touches the same five modules?

turns.user: Can you look at this subsystem and tell me whether the design is the reason every change touches the same five modules?
Option B sounds right. Now work out the sequence for making that change.
Okay, implement the first approved phase.

cases.notes: Workflow ownership must move from review to planning; the agent must not stay in the review skill. The final turn is ordinary implementation: no skill in the set owns generic implementation (implementation-planning explicitly stops before editing code), so expected_route null means 'no specialized skill expected'.

cases.prompt: The reports/generator.py file is a 2500-line god file. Split it into cohesive modules along ownership boundaries without changing behavior.
cases.notes: Architecture vocabulary (ownership boundaries) but the deliverable is a behavior-preserving split of one file.

cases.prompt: We approved the auth token-refresh design last quarter, but since then we upgraded the framework and moved session storage to Redis. Produce the execution-ready plan from that approved design.
cases.notes: Drift-check + planning in one message; the plan from the approved design is the dominant job.

cases.prompt: We shipped the export endpoint with zero tests for empty input, malformed JSON, duplicate deliveries, and idempotency. Run a QA pass: add regression coverage for those gaps and fix anything broken.
cases.notes: Not a code review (no findings report requested) and not planning; the deliverable is test-first coverage plus minimal fixes.
